title: ‘Those two jobs need different physics’: Rebellions CEO says training and inference need different chips
excerpt: Model training still needs flagship chips, but could inference get away with lighter chips?
content_html:
The AI race started off with a pretty clear direction – bigger and better. The first waves were characterized by building bigger models, but it’s all change in the world of artificial intelligence and with enterprises, SMBs and consumers all finding use cases for the technology, the focus has shifted.

Now, AI firms and model developers are looking to realize a much tougher goal. Efficiency. Cost per token, performance per watt, output per input, it’s all about driving maximum efficiency.

One clear divide is between training and inference. While training models still requires huge amounts of resources, inference efficiency is starting to improve, and one company (Rebellions) now believes an opening for inference-first hardware could create a new market.

The company’s racks are said to consume around 16-20kW, compared with around 120kW for leading GPU-based inference systems that, for many use cases, are sheer overkill.

Rebellions’ rack costs are also said to be around one-third of the price, making AI inference more accessible and helping enterprises to deploy AI more widely.

This hardware shift could be the start of truly efficient AI

Memory is also another battleground, whereby huge trillion-parameter models are testing the limits of today’s hardware and the intertwined reliance on memory and compute. Something Rebellions is looking to fix by working with memory and foundry partners to align multiple roadmaps, instead of having to respond to shifts in architecture.

Ultimately, today’s black-and-white chip manufacturing landscape is now evolving, and Rebellions sees two key changes happening simultaneously. Firstly, training and inference hardware is starting to differ more drastically. Secondly, aligning multiple hardware roadmaps across memory, compute and more will drive more efficiency not just across deployments, but in terms of bringing new products to market.

I spoke to Rebellions CEO Sunghyun Park allows me to understand how and why inference and training hardware are starting to separate, as well as the importance of open standards and collaboration in the drive for all-round efficiency.

  • The AI chip market seems to be splitting between training-first and inference-first architectures. Why is that happening, and why now?

This split exists because training and inference are fundamentally different problems.

Training is how you build a model. It happens once, involves a small number of organizations, and rewards raw computational flexibility because the workload keeps shifting as research moves forward.

Inference is how you actually use a model: every query answered, every transaction processed, every decision an AI system makes in production. That happens billions of times a day across nearly every industry, and it’s where AI moves from R&D into revenue.

Those two jobs need different physics. Training requires maximum FLOPS. Inference requires efficiency, reliability, and economics that hold up when you’re serving users at scale.

The industry forced a training chip into that second job because that’s what existed. Now that inference has become the larger, more urgent market, that compromise no longer holds. Enterprises and governments are asking how fast they can deploy. That’s why the conversation is splitting now.

  • Where does Rebellions fit in that split, and what makes your approach to AI inference fundamentally different from your competitors?

We built for inference, from day one. Most first-generation AI chip companies emerged from the 2016-2017 training boom and adapted their architectures for inference afterward.

We started in 2020 – after that wave – with inference as the only target, which meant designing around what production AI actually needs instead of retrofitting a training chip.

The numbers reflect that choice. Our racks draw 16-20kW versus roughly 120kW for leading GPU-based inference systems, about a sixth of the power, in a market where power is the binding constraint for most operators.

Acquisition cost runs around $10 million per rack versus roughly $30 million, about a third of the cost. Our chiplet-based architecture also scales out rather than betting that a single device can handle a model’s full size, which matters now that production workloads are trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models instead of the few-hundred-million-parameter models the first generation was built around.

It’s also why our architecture is memory-centric rather than compute-centric. The chiplet approach exists to keep memory close to logic as models scale, not just to add cores.

And we have three years of production deployments behind that architecture, not pilots. That’s the hardest part to replicate: real workloads, running at scale, today.

  • A year ago, everyone in AI was talking about chiplets. Now the conversation has shifted to memory. What changed?

The chiplet conversation was about architecture: breaking a chip into modular pieces that scale independently, rather than betting everything on a single monolithic die.

That mattered because it let the industry move past an assumption the first generation of accelerators made in 2016 and 2017, that a single device would always be big enough to run any model.

That assumption broke once mixture-of-experts and trillion-parameter models arrived.

The memory conversation is the layer underneath that. Once the architecture problem is solved, the constraint becomes physical: can you actually get enough high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to build what you’ve designed?

HBM is 3D-stacked memory, and how closely you can physically stack it to compute is as much of a bottleneck as raw supply.

Every AI accelerator company is competing for the same limited supply right now, and demand has outpaced what memory makers can produce. That’s the memory-logic co-design problem: architecture and memory supply are no longer separable decisions.

We’re in a different position because our investor relationships were built around supply, not just capital. Our memory partners are also investors, and we co-design our memory architecture directly against their roadmaps rather than simply purchasing off them.

Our chiplet architecture also develops against our foundry partner’s process roadmap. When the rest of the industry was fighting for allocation, we already had a seat at the design table through those relationships.

That’s memory-logic co-design, not just secured supply. The shift from chiplets to memory tracks has moved the real constraint: from architecture to physical supply.

  • Your stack runs on open-source frameworks like vLLM, PyTorch, Kubernetes, and OpenShift, tools many enterprises already use. Does that make adoption relatively plug-and-play, or is that an oversimplification?

It’s mostly true, but ‘plug-and-play’ undersells how deliberate that was, and oversimplifies in one specific way.

We built entirely on open standards: vLLM, PyTorch, Kubernetes, and Red Hat OpenShift. We’re one of only two chip companies in the PyTorch Foundation, and the only AI accelerator company fully integrated with OpenShift.

A developer who already knows how to run inference on existing infrastructure already knows how to run it on ours. There’s no proprietary runtime to learn and no migration project. That part really is close to plug-and-play.

The first generation of AI chip companies each built proprietary software stacks, and hundreds of millions of dollars went into software that didn’t survive. We came to market once the open source ecosystem had matured and chose to build on it instead of forking it.

Where it oversimplifies is assuming that means zero integration work. Production deployments still require validating performance at your specific workload and scale, and that takes real engineering time, no matter how compatible the stack is.

What open standards remove is lock-in risk and retraining cost, not the deployment work itself.

  • What are the biggest challenges organizations face when trying to run AI inference outside of hyperscaler platforms?

Most organizations aren’t built like hyperscalers, and much of the available inference infrastructure assumes they are.

The first challenge is physical. Most enterprises, telcos, and governments already have data centers. They can’t wait two to three years or spend $600 million-plus on new ones, and they can’t retrofit for liquid cooling without major cost and disruption.

So the practical question is whether inference hardware runs on what they already have: standard racks, air cooling, and existing power budgets.

The second is sovereignty. Organizations increasingly want to bring compute to where their data already lives, rather than move sensitive data to wherever compute is hosted.

That’s partly regulatory, partly operational, but either way, cloud-only inference creates a dependency a lot of operators are no longer comfortable with.

We built specifically for that gap. Our systems run at 4-5kW per server on standard air-cooled infrastructure, no facility redesign required.

SK Telecom has run on our hardware for nearly three years, scaling from a small cluster to close to 100 racks and now processing 50 million API transactions a day, entirely inside their existing network.

KT Cloud runs real-time inference on highway CCTV systems nationally. Both show you don’t need hyperscaler-scale infrastructure to run AI at hyperscaler-relevant volume.

  • Cerebras' IPO, and potential listings from others in the space, have put AI infrastructure in the spotlight. What do these IPOs signal about the market, and where might the hype be outpacing deployment reality?

It tells the public markets that AI infrastructure is a durable, investable asset class, not just a venture-backed bet. That validation benefits the whole sector, including us: it says purpose-built AI silicon is real, differentiated from general-purpose GPUs, and worth independent capital.

Capital flowing into the sector is necessary, but it doesn’t by itself determine who wins. The companies that define the next decade of this market won’t necessarily be the most-funded ones.

They’ll be the ones with real fundamentals: production customers, deployment scale, proven economics, durable supply chain relationships. That’s a different filter than fundraising size, and it’s the one that matters once public market scrutiny starts.

We’ve been building toward that filter since 2020, with production deployments and supply relationships with our foundry and memory partners that we secured before the rest of the industry was fighting over the same allocation. The capital is a tailwind for everyone serious about inference.

Whether it gets deployed well is a separate question, and one the market will answer over the next few years.

  • Looking ahead, what trends are you watching most closely across AI infrastructure and inference over the next 12–24 months?

The buildout happening inside existing infrastructure keeps accelerating. Most enterprises, telcos, and governments aren’t waiting for new data centers.

They’re deploying inference into facilities they already have, and I expect that to become the bigger story even though it gets less attention than hyperscaler headlines.

Additionally, memory remains the physical constraint. HBM supply hasn’t caught up with demand, and as models keep moving toward trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architectures, that pressure increases rather than eases.

Companies with secured, strategic supply relationships will have a real advantage over the next two years, not just a cost one.

Chiplets are how we get there. We’ve already mass-produced a highly advanced 4-chiplet package – a level of integration Nvidia has struggled to reach.

Reporting this year indicated Nvidia had built and demonstrated a four-chiplet Rubin Ultra design, then canceled it in favor of a dual-die architecture over manufacturability concerns: a four-die single package pushes roughly 7.5-8x past reticle limits on yield and cost. That’s the foundation.

The next layer we’re building on is performance optimization of HMB3E (3D-stacked memory) in close collaboration with memory and compute co-designed together from the start, not bolted on after the fact.

Also on my radar is the fact that as more companies in this space go public, capital will get valued against production fundamentals rather than funding rounds.

And the efficiency point matters: as inference gets cheaper per token, demand doesn’t shrink, it expands, because new use cases become viable at lower cost. That’s been true of every computing platform in history, and I don’t expect AI inference to be the exception.

blocks.html_en: Inference is how you actually use a model: every query answered, every transaction processed, every decision an AI system makes in production. That happens billions of times a day across nearly every industry, and it’s where AI moves from R&D into revenue.

sentences.en: Inference is how you actually use a model: every query answered, every transaction processed, every decision an AI system makes in production.
sentences.zh: 推理是您实际使用模型的方式：回答每个查询、处理每个事务、人工智能系统在生产中做出的每个决策。

sentences.en: That happens billions of times a day across nearly every industry, and it’s where AI moves from R&D into revenue.
sentences.zh: 这种情况每天在几乎每个行业发生数十亿次，这也是人工智能从研发转化为收入的地方。

blocks.html_en: Those two jobs need different physics. Training requires maximum FLOPS. Inference requires efficiency, reliability, and economics that hold up when you’re serving users at scale.

sentences.en: Those two jobs need different physics.
sentences.zh: 这两项工作需要不同的物理原理。

sentences.en: Training requires maximum FLOPS.
sentences.zh: 训练需要最大的 FLOPS。

sentences.en: Inference requires efficiency, reliability, and economics that hold up when you’re serving users at scale.
sentences.zh: 推理需要在为大规模用户提供服务时保持高效、可靠性和经济性。

blocks.html_en: The industry forced a training chip into that second job because that’s what existed. Now that inference has become the larger, more urgent market, that compromise no longer holds. Enterprises and governments are asking how fast they can deploy. That’s why the conversation is splitting now.

sentences.en: The industry forced a training chip into that second job because that’s what existed.
sentences.zh: 该行业将培训芯片强加到第二项工作中，因为这就是现有的。

sentences.en: Now that inference has become the larger, more urgent market, that compromise no longer holds.
sentences.zh: 现在推理已经成为更大、更紧迫的市场，这种妥协不再成立。

sentences.en: Enterprises and governments are asking how fast they can deploy.
sentences.zh: 企业和政府都在询问他们的部署速度有多快。

sentences.en: That’s why the conversation is splitting now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么现在谈话出现分歧。

blocks.html_en: • Where does Rebellions fit in that split, and what makes your approach to AI inference fundamentally different from your competitors?

sentences.en: Where does Rebellions fit in that split, and what makes your approach to AI inference fundamentally different from your competitors?
sentences.zh: Rebellions 在这种分裂中处于什么位置？是什么让你们的人工智能推理方法与竞争对手有根本不同？

blocks.html_en: We built for inference, from day one. Most first-generation AI chip companies emerged from the 2016-2017 training boom and adapted their architectures for inference afterward.

sentences.en: We built for inference, from day one.
sentences.zh: 从第一天起，我们就为推理而构建。

sentences.en: Most first-generation AI chip companies emerged from the 2016-2017 training boom and adapted their architectures for inference afterward.
sentences.zh: 大多数第一代人工智能芯片公司都是从 2016-2017 年的培训热潮中崛起的，并随后调整了其推理架构。

blocks.html_en: We started in 2020 – after that wave – with inference as the only target, which meant designing around what production AI actually needs instead of retrofitting a training chip.

sentences.en: We started in 2020 – after that wave – with inference as the only target, which meant designing around what production AI actually needs instead of retrofitting a training chip.
sentences.zh: 我们从 2020 年开始——在那波浪潮之后——以推理为唯一目标，这意味着围绕生产 AI 实际需要进行设计，而不是改造训练芯片。

blocks.html_en: The numbers reflect that choice. Our racks draw 16-20kW versus roughly 120kW for leading GPU-based inference systems, about a sixth of the power, in a market where power is the binding constraint for most operators.

sentences.en: The numbers reflect that choice.
sentences.zh: 这些数字反映了这种选择。

sentences.en: Our racks draw 16-20kW versus roughly 120kW for leading GPU-based inference systems, about a sixth of the power, in a market where power is the binding constraint for most operators.
sentences.zh: 我们的机架消耗 16-20kW 的功率，而领先的基于 GPU 的推理系统的功率约为 120kW，约为功率的六分之一，在功率是大多数运营商的约束性限制的市场中。

blocks.html_en: Acquisition cost runs around $10 million per rack versus roughly $30 million, about a third of the cost. Our chiplet-based architecture also scales out rather than betting that a single device can handle a model’s full size, which matters now that production workloads are trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models instead of the few-hundred-million-parameter models the first generation was built around.

sentences.en: Acquisition cost runs around $10 million per rack versus roughly $30 million, about a third of the cost.
sentences.zh: 每个机架的购置成本约为 1000 万美元，而每个机架的购置成本约为 3000 万美元，约占成本的三分之一。

sentences.en: Our chiplet-based architecture also scales out rather than betting that a single device can handle a model’s full size, which matters now that production workloads are trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models instead of the few-hundred-million-parameter models the first generation was built around.
sentences.zh: 我们基于小芯片的架构还可以横向扩展，而不是押注于单个设备可以处理模型的全尺寸，这一点很重要，因为生产工作负载是数万亿参数的专家混合模型，而不是第一代围绕的数亿参数模型。

blocks.html_en: It’s also why our architecture is memory-centric rather than compute-centric. The chiplet approach exists to keep memory close to logic as models scale, not just to add cores.

sentences.en: It’s also why our architecture is memory-centric rather than compute-centric.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我们的架构以内存为中心而不是以计算为中心的原因。

sentences.en: The chiplet approach exists to keep memory close to logic as models scale, not just to add cores.
sentences.zh: 小芯片方法的存在是为了在模型扩展时保持内存接近逻辑，而不仅仅是添加内核。

blocks.html_en: And we have three years of production deployments behind that architecture, not pilots. That’s the hardest part to replicate: real workloads, running at scale, today.

sentences.en: And we have three years of production deployments behind that architecture, not pilots.
sentences.zh: 我们对该架构进行了三年的生产部署，而不是试点。

sentences.en: That’s the hardest part to replicate: real workloads, running at scale, today.
sentences.zh: 这是最难复制的部分：当今大规模运行的真实工作负载。

blocks.html_en: • A year ago, everyone in AI was talking about chiplets. Now the conversation has shifted to memory. What changed?

sentences.en: A year ago, everyone in AI was talking about chiplets.
sentences.zh: 一年前，人工智能领域的每个人都在谈论小芯片。

sentences.en: Now the conversation has shifted to memory.
sentences.zh: 现在谈话已经转移到记忆中。

sentences.en: What changed?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么变化？

blocks.html_en: The chiplet conversation was about architecture: breaking a chip into modular pieces that scale independently, rather than betting everything on a single monolithic die.

sentences.en: The chiplet conversation was about architecture: breaking a chip into modular pieces that scale independently, rather than betting everything on a single monolithic die.
sentences.zh: Chiplet 的讨论是关于架构的：将芯片分解为可独立扩展的模块化部件，而不是将所有内容都押在单个单片芯片上。

blocks.html_en: That mattered because it let the industry move past an assumption the first generation of accelerators made in 2016 and 2017, that a single device would always be big enough to run any model.

sentences.en: That mattered because it let the industry move past an assumption the first generation of accelerators made in 2016 and 2017, that a single device would always be big enough to run any model.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为它让行业摆脱了 2016 年和 2017 年第一代加速器的假设，即单个设备始终足够大以运行任何模型。

blocks.html_en: That assumption broke once mixture-of-experts and trillion-parameter models arrived.

sentences.en: That assumption broke once mixture-of-experts and trillion-parameter models arrived.
sentences.zh: 一旦专家混合模型和万亿参数模型出现，这种假设就被打破了。

blocks.html_en: The memory conversation is the layer underneath that. Once the architecture problem is solved, the constraint becomes physical: can you actually get enough high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to build what you’ve designed?

sentences.en: The memory conversation is the layer underneath that.
sentences.zh: 记忆对话是其之下的一层。

sentences.en: Once the architecture problem is solved, the constraint becomes physical: can you actually get enough high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to build what you’ve designed?
sentences.zh: 一旦架构问题得到解决，约束就变成了物理上的：您实际上可以获得足够的高带宽内存（HBM）来构建您所设计的内容吗？

blocks.html_en: HBM is 3D-stacked memory, and how closely you can physically stack it to compute is as much of a bottleneck as raw supply.

sentences.en: HBM is 3D-stacked memory, and how closely you can physically stack it to compute is as much of a bottleneck as raw supply.
sentences.zh: HBM 是 3D 堆叠内存，其物理堆叠与计算的紧密程度与原始供应一样是一个瓶颈。

blocks.html_en: Every AI accelerator company is competing for the same limited supply right now, and demand has outpaced what memory makers can produce. That’s the memory-logic co-design problem: architecture and memory supply are no longer separable decisions.

sentences.en: Every AI accelerator company is competing for the same limited supply right now, and demand has outpaced what memory makers can produce.
sentences.zh: 目前，每家人工智能加速器公司都在争夺同样有限的供应，而需求已经超过了内存制造商的生产能力。

sentences.en: That’s the memory-logic co-design problem: architecture and memory supply are no longer separable decisions.
sentences.zh: 这就是内存逻辑协同设计问题：架构和内存供应不再是可分离的决策。

blocks.html_en: We’re in a different position because our investor relationships were built around supply, not just capital. Our memory partners are also investors, and we co-design our memory architecture directly against their roadmaps rather than simply purchasing off them.

sentences.en: We’re in a different position because our investor relationships were built around supply, not just capital.
sentences.zh: 我们的处境不同，因为我们的投资者关系是围绕供应而不仅仅是资本建立的。

sentences.en: Our memory partners are also investors, and we co-design our memory architecture directly against their roadmaps rather than simply purchasing off them.
sentences.zh: 我们的内存合作伙伴也是投资者，我们直接根据他们的路线图共同设计我们的内存架构，而不是简单地从他们那里购买。

blocks.html_en: Our chiplet architecture also develops against our foundry partner’s process roadmap. When the rest of the industry was fighting for allocation, we already had a seat at the design table through those relationships.

sentences.en: Our chiplet architecture also develops against our foundry partner’s process roadmap.
sentences.zh: 我们的小芯片架构也是根据我们的代工合作伙伴的工艺路线图开发的。

sentences.en: When the rest of the industry was fighting for allocation, we already had a seat at the design table through those relationships.
sentences.zh: 当行业的其他公司都在争夺分配时，我们已经通过这些关系在设计桌上占据了一席之地。

blocks.html_en: That’s memory-logic co-design, not just secured supply. The shift from chiplets to memory tracks has moved the real constraint: from architecture to physical supply.

sentences.en: That’s memory-logic co-design, not just secured supply.
sentences.zh: 这是内存逻辑协同设计，而不仅仅是安全供应。

sentences.en: The shift from chiplets to memory tracks has moved the real constraint: from architecture to physical supply.
sentences.zh: 从小芯片到内存轨道的转变已经转移了真正的限制：从架构到物理供应。

blocks.html_en: • Your stack runs on open-source frameworks like vLLM, PyTorch, Kubernetes, and OpenShift, tools many enterprises already use. Does that make adoption relatively plug-and-play, or is that an oversimplification?

sentences.en: Your stack runs on open-source frameworks like vLLM, PyTorch, Kubernetes, and OpenShift, tools many enterprises already use.
sentences.zh: 您的堆栈在 vLLM、PyTorch、Kubernetes 和 OpenShift 等开源框架上运行，这些工具是许多企业已经使用的工具。

sentences.en: Does that make adoption relatively plug-and-play, or is that an oversimplification?
sentences.zh: 这是否使得采用相对即插即用，或者是否过于简单化了？

blocks.html_en: It’s mostly true, but ‘plug-and-play’ undersells how deliberate that was, and oversimplifies in one specific way.

sentences.en: It’s mostly true, but ‘plug-and-play’ undersells how deliberate that was, and oversimplifies in one specific way.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是正确的，但“即插即用”低估了这是多么深思熟虑，并且在一种特定的方式上过于简单化。

blocks.html_en: We built entirely on open standards: vLLM, PyTorch, Kubernetes, and Red Hat OpenShift. We’re one of only two chip companies in the PyTorch Foundation, and the only AI accelerator company fully integrated with OpenShift.

sentences.en: We built entirely on open standards: vLLM, PyTorch, Kubernetes, and Red Hat OpenShift.
sentences.zh: 我们完全基于开放标准构建：vLLM、PyTorch、Kubernetes 和 Red Hat OpenShift。

sentences.en: We’re one of only two chip companies in the PyTorch Foundation, and the only AI accelerator company fully integrated with OpenShift.
sentences.zh: 我们是 PyTorch 基金会仅有的两家芯片公司之一，也是唯一一家与 OpenShift 完全集成的 AI 加速器公司。

blocks.html_en: A developer who already knows how to run inference on existing infrastructure already knows how to run it on ours. There’s no proprietary runtime to learn and no migration project. That part really is close to plug-and-play.

sentences.en: A developer who already knows how to run inference on existing infrastructure already knows how to run it on ours.
sentences.zh: 已经知道如何在现有基础设施上运行推理的开发人员也知道如何在我们的基础设施上运行它。

sentences.en: There’s no proprietary runtime to learn and no migration project.
sentences.zh: 没有专有的运行时可供学习，也没有迁移项目。

sentences.en: That part really is close to plug-and-play.
sentences.zh: 这部分确实接近于即插即用。

blocks.html_en: The first generation of AI chip companies each built proprietary software stacks, and hundreds of millions of dollars went into software that didn’t survive. We came to market once the open source ecosystem had matured and chose to build on it instead of forking it.

sentences.en: The first generation of AI chip companies each built proprietary software stacks, and hundreds of millions of dollars went into software that didn’t survive.
sentences.zh: 第一代人工智能芯片公司各自构建了专有的软件堆栈，数亿美元投入到了无法生存的软件中。

sentences.en: We came to market once the open source ecosystem had matured and chose to build on it instead of forking it.
sentences.zh: 当开源生态系统成熟后，我们就进入了市场，并选择在它的基础上进行构建，而不是分叉它。

blocks.html_en: Where it oversimplifies is assuming that means zero integration work. Production deployments still require validating performance at your specific workload and scale, and that takes real engineering time, no matter how compatible the stack is.

sentences.en: Where it oversimplifies is assuming that means zero integration work.
sentences.zh: 它过于简单化的地方是假设这意味着零集成工作。

sentences.en: Production deployments still require validating performance at your specific workload and scale, and that takes real engineering time, no matter how compatible the stack is.
sentences.zh: 生产部署仍然需要验证特定工作负载和规模的性能，并且无论堆栈的兼容性如何，这都需要真正的工程时间。

blocks.html_en: What open standards remove is lock-in risk and retraining cost, not the deployment work itself.

sentences.en: What open standards remove is lock-in risk and retraining cost, not the deployment work itself.
sentences.zh: 开放标准消除的是锁定风险和再培训成本，而不是部署工作本身。

blocks.html_en: • What are the biggest challenges organizations face when trying to run AI inference outside of hyperscaler platforms?

sentences.en: What are the biggest challenges organizations face when trying to run AI inference outside of hyperscaler platforms?
sentences.zh: 组织尝试在超大规模平台之外运行人工智能推理时面临的最大挑战是什么？

blocks.html_en: Most organizations aren’t built like hyperscalers, and much of the available inference infrastructure assumes they are.

sentences.en: Most organizations aren’t built like hyperscalers, and much of the available inference infrastructure assumes they are.
sentences.zh: 大多数组织并不是像超大规模企业那样构建的，而且许多可用的推理基础设施都假设它们是这样的。

blocks.html_en: The first challenge is physical. Most enterprises, telcos, and governments already have data centers. They can’t wait two to three years or spend $600 million-plus on new ones, and they can’t retrofit for liquid cooling without major cost and disruption.

sentences.en: The first challenge is physical.
sentences.zh: 第一个挑战是身体上的。

sentences.en: Most enterprises, telcos, and governments already have data centers.
sentences.zh: 大多数企业、电信公司和政府已经拥有数据中心。

sentences.en: They can’t wait two to three years or spend $600 million-plus on new ones, and they can’t retrofit for liquid cooling without major cost and disruption.
sentences.zh: 他们不能等待两到三年，也不能花费 6 亿多美元购买新设备，而且他们无法在不付出重大成本和中断的情况下进行液体冷却改造。

blocks.html_en: So the practical question is whether inference hardware runs on what they already have: standard racks, air cooling, and existing power budgets.

sentences.en: So the practical question is whether inference hardware runs on what they already have: standard racks, air cooling, and existing power budgets.
sentences.zh: 因此，实际的问题是推理硬件是否运行在他们已有的基础上：标准机架、空气冷却和现有的功率预算。

blocks.html_en: The second is sovereignty. Organizations increasingly want to bring compute to where their data already lives, rather than move sensitive data to wherever compute is hosted.

sentences.en: The second is sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 第二是主权。

sentences.en: Organizations increasingly want to bring compute to where their data already lives, rather than move sensitive data to wherever compute is hosted.
sentences.zh: 组织越来越希望将计算带到数据已经存在的地方，而不是将敏感数据移动到托管计算的地方。

blocks.html_en: That’s partly regulatory, partly operational, but either way, cloud-only inference creates a dependency a lot of operators are no longer comfortable with.

sentences.en: That’s partly regulatory, partly operational, but either way, cloud-only inference creates a dependency a lot of operators are no longer comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 这部分是监管性的，部分是运营性的，但无论哪种方式，仅云推理都会造成许多运营商不再适应的依赖。

blocks.html_en: We built specifically for that gap. Our systems run at 4-5kW per server on standard air-cooled infrastructure, no facility redesign required.

sentences.en: We built specifically for that gap.
sentences.zh: 我们专门针对这一差距而构建。

sentences.en: Our systems run at 4-5kW per server on standard air-cooled infrastructure, no facility redesign required.
sentences.zh: 我们的系统在标准风冷基础设施上以每台服务器 4-5kW 的功率运行，无需重新设计设施。

blocks.html_en: SK Telecom has run on our hardware for nearly three years, scaling from a small cluster to close to 100 racks and now processing 50 million API transactions a day, entirely inside their existing network.

sentences.en: SK Telecom has run on our hardware for nearly three years, scaling from a small cluster to close to 100 racks and now processing 50 million API transactions a day, entirely inside their existing network.
sentences.zh: SK Telecom 在我们的硬件上运行了近三年，从一个小型集群扩展到接近 100 个机架，现在每天处理 5000 万个 API 事务，完全在其现有网络内进行。

blocks.html_en: KT Cloud runs real-time inference on highway CCTV systems nationally. Both show you don’t need hyperscaler-scale infrastructure to run AI at hyperscaler-relevant volume.

sentences.en: KT Cloud runs real-time inference on highway CCTV systems nationally.
sentences.zh: KT Cloud 在全国高速公路闭路电视系统上运行实时推理。

sentences.en: Both show you don’t need hyperscaler-scale infrastructure to run AI at hyperscaler-relevant volume.
sentences.zh: 两者都表明，您不需要超大规模的基础设施来以超大规模相关的数量运行人工智能。

blocks.html_en: • Cerebras' IPO, and potential listings from others in the space, have put AI infrastructure in the spotlight. What do these IPOs signal about the market, and where might the hype be outpacing deployment reality?

sentences.en: Cerebras' IPO, and potential listings from others in the space, have put AI infrastructure in the spotlight.
sentences.zh: Cerebras 的 IPO 以及该领域其他公司的潜在上市，使人工智能基础设施成为人们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: What do these IPOs signal about the market, and where might the hype be outpacing deployment reality?
sentences.zh: 这些首次公开募股向市场发出了什么信号？炒作可能在哪些方面超过部署现实？

blocks.html_en: It tells the public markets that AI infrastructure is a durable, investable asset class, not just a venture-backed bet. That validation benefits the whole sector, including us: it says purpose-built AI silicon is real, differentiated from general-purpose GPUs, and worth independent capital.

sentences.en: It tells the public markets that AI infrastructure is a durable, investable asset class, not just a venture-backed bet.
sentences.zh: 它告诉公开市场，人工智能基础设施是一种持久的、可投资的资产类别，而不仅仅是风险投资支持的赌注。

sentences.en: That validation benefits the whole sector, including us: it says purpose-built AI silicon is real, differentiated from general-purpose GPUs, and worth independent capital.
sentences.zh: 这种验证有利于整个行业，包括我们：它表明专用人工智能芯片是真实的，与通用 GPU 不同，并且值得独立资本。

blocks.html_en: Capital flowing into the sector is necessary, but it doesn’t by itself determine who wins. The companies that define the next decade of this market won’t necessarily be the most-funded ones.

sentences.en: Capital flowing into the sector is necessary, but it doesn’t by itself determine who wins.
sentences.zh: 资本流入该行业是必要的，但它本身并不能决定谁会获胜。

sentences.en: The companies that define the next decade of this market won’t necessarily be the most-funded ones.
sentences.zh: 定义这个市场下一个十年的公司不一定是资金最多的公司。

blocks.html_en: They’ll be the ones with real fundamentals: production customers, deployment scale, proven economics, durable supply chain relationships. That’s a different filter than fundraising size, and it’s the one that matters once public market scrutiny starts.

sentences.en: They’ll be the ones with real fundamentals: production customers, deployment scale, proven economics, durable supply chain relationships.
sentences.zh: 他们将是具有真正基础的人：生产客户、部署规模、经过验证的经济性、持久的供应链关系。

sentences.en: That’s a different filter than fundraising size, and it’s the one that matters once public market scrutiny starts.
sentences.zh: 这是与筹款规模不同的过滤器，一旦公开市场审查开始，这才是重要的。

blocks.html_en: We’ve been building toward that filter since 2020, with production deployments and supply relationships with our foundry and memory partners that we secured before the rest of the industry was fighting over the same allocation. The capital is a tailwind for everyone serious about inference.

sentences.en: We’ve been building toward that filter since 2020, with production deployments and supply relationships with our foundry and memory partners that we secured before the rest of the industry was fighting over the same allocation.
sentences.zh: 自 2020 年以来，我们一直在朝着这个目标迈进，在行业其他公司争夺同样的分配之前，我们就与代工厂和内存合作伙伴建立了生产部署和供应关系。

sentences.en: The capital is a tailwind for everyone serious about inference.
sentences.zh: 对于每个认真推理的人来说，首都都是顺风。

blocks.html_en: Whether it gets deployed well is a separate question, and one the market will answer over the next few years.

content_html_zh:
人工智能竞赛一开始就有一个非常明确的方向——更大、更好。 第一波浪潮的特点是构建更大的模型，但这一切都发生在人工智能世界中，随着企业、中小企业和消费者都在寻找该技术的用例，焦点已经转移。

现在，人工智能公司和模型开发人员正在寻求实现一个更加艰巨的目标。 效率。 每个代币的成本、每瓦特的性能、每输入的输出，这一切都是为了提高效率。

训练和推理之间存在一个明显的区别。 虽然训练模型仍然需要大量资源，但推理效率正在开始提高，一家公司（Rebellions）现在认为推理优先硬件的开放可以创造一个新市场。

据称，该公司的机架功耗约为 16-20kW，而领先的基于 GPU 的推理系统的功耗约为 120kW，对于许多用例来说，这完全是多余的。

据称，Rebellions 的机架成本也仅为其价格的三分之一左右，使人工智能推理变得更容易实现，并帮助企业更广泛地部署人工智能。

这种硬件转变可能是真正高效人工智能的开始

内存也是另一个战场，数万亿参数的巨大模型正在测试当今硬件的极限以及对内存和计算的相互依赖。 Rebellions 正在寻求通过与内存和代工合作伙伴合作来协调多个路线图来解决问题，而不是必须应对架构的变化。

最终，当今的黑白芯片制造格局正在不断发展，Rebellions 看到两个关键变化同时发生。 首先，训练和推理硬件开始出现更大的差异。 其次，跨内存、计算等调整多个硬件路线图不仅可以提高部署效率，还可以提高新产品推向市场的效率。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

我与 Rebellions 首席执行官 Sunghyun Park 的交谈让我了解了推理和训练硬件如何以及为何开始分离，以及开放标准和协作在推动全面效率方面的重要性。

  • 人工智能芯片市场似乎正在分为训练优先和推理优先的架构。 为什么会发生这种情况，为什么是现在？

这种分歧的存在是因为训练和推理是根本不同的问题。

训练是构建模型的方式。 它发生一次，涉及少数组织，并奖励原始的计算灵活性，因为工作量随着研究的进展而不断变化。

推理是您实际使用模型的方式：回答每个查询、处理每个事务、人工智能系统在生产中做出的每个决策。 这种情况每天在几乎每个行业发生数十亿次，这也是人工智能从研发转化为收入的地方。

这两项工作需要不同的物理原理。 训练需要最大的 FLOPS。 推理需要在为大规模用户提供服务时保持高效、可靠性和经济性。

该行业将培训芯片强加到第二项工作中，因为这就是现有的。 现在推理已经成为更大、更紧迫的市场，这种妥协不再成立。 企业和政府都在询问他们的部署速度有多快。 这就是为什么现在谈话出现分歧。

  • Rebellions 在这种分裂中处于什么位置？是什么让你们的人工智能推理方法与竞争对手有根本不同？

从第一天起，我们就为推理而构建。 大多数第一代人工智能芯片公司都是从 2016-2017 年的培训热潮中崛起的，并随后调整了其推理架构。

我们从 2020 年开始——在那波浪潮之后——以推理为唯一目标，这意味着围绕生产 AI 实际需要进行设计，而不是改造训练芯片。

这些数字反映了这种选择。 我们的机架消耗 16-20kW 的功率，而领先的基于 GPU 的推理系统的功率约为 120kW，约为功率的六分之一，在功率是大多数运营商的约束性限制的市场中。

每个机架的购置成本约为 1000 万美元，而每个机架的购置成本约为 3000 万美元，约占成本的三分之一。 我们基于小芯片的架构还可以横向扩展，而不是押注于单个设备可以处理模型的全尺寸，这一点很重要，因为生产工作负载是数万亿参数的专家混合模型，而不是第一代围绕的数亿参数模型。

这也是为什么我们的架构以内存为中心而不是以计算为中心的原因。 小芯片方法的存在是为了在模型扩展时保持内存接近逻辑，而不仅仅是添加内核。

我们对该架构进行了三年的生产部署，而不是试点。 这是最难复制的部分：当今大规模运行的真实工作负载。

  • 一年前，人工智能领域的每个人都在谈论小芯片。 现在谈话已经转移到记忆中。 发生了什么变化？

Chiplet 的讨论是关于架构的：将芯片分解为可独立扩展的模块化部件，而不是将所有内容都押在单个单片芯片上。

这很重要，因为它让行业摆脱了 2016 年和 2017 年第一代加速器的假设，即单个设备始终足够大以运行任何模型。

一旦专家混合模型和万亿参数模型出现，这种假设就被打破了。

记忆对话是其之下的一层。 一旦架构问题得到解决，约束就变成了物理上的：您实际上可以获得足够的高带宽内存（HBM）来构建您所设计的内容吗？

HBM 是 3D 堆叠内存，其物理堆叠与计算的紧密程度与原始供应一样是一个瓶颈。

目前，每家人工智能加速器公司都在争夺同样有限的供应，而需求已经超过了内存制造商的生产能力。 这就是内存逻辑协同设计问题：架构和内存供应不再是可分离的决策。

我们的处境不同，因为我们的投资者关系是围绕供应而不仅仅是资本建立的。 我们的内存合作伙伴也是投资者，我们直接根据他们的路线图共同设计我们的内存架构，而不是简单地从他们那里购买。

我们的小芯片架构也是根据我们的代工合作伙伴的工艺路线图开发的。 当行业的其他公司都在争夺分配时，我们已经通过这些关系在设计桌上占据了一席之地。

这是内存逻辑协同设计，而不仅仅是安全供应。 从小芯片到内存轨道的转变已经转移了真正的限制：从架构到物理供应。

  • 您的堆栈在 vLLM、PyTorch、Kubernetes 和 OpenShift 等开源框架上运行，这些工具是许多企业已经使用的工具。 这是否使得采用相对即插即用，或者是否过于简单化了？

这基本上是正确的，但“即插即用”低估了这是多么深思熟虑，并且在一种特定的方式上过于简单化。

我们完全基于开放标准构建：vLLM、PyTorch、Kubernetes 和 Red Hat OpenShift。 我们是 PyTorch 基金会仅有的两家芯片公司之一，也是唯一一家与 OpenShift 完全集成的 AI 加速器公司。

已经知道如何在现有基础设施上运行推理的开发人员也知道如何在我们的基础设施上运行它。 没有专有的运行时可供学习，也没有迁移项目。 这部分确实接近于即插即用。

第一代人工智能芯片公司各自构建了专有的软件堆栈，数亿美元投入到了无法生存的软件中。 当开源生态系统成熟后，我们就进入了市场，并选择在它的基础上进行构建，而不是分叉它。

它过于简单化的地方是假设这意味着零集成工作。 生产部署仍然需要验证特定工作负载和规模的性能，并且无论堆栈的兼容性如何，这都需要真正的工程时间。

开放标准消除的是锁定风险和再培训成本，而不是部署工作本身。

  • 组织尝试在超大规模平台之外运行人工智能推理时面临的最大挑战是什么？

大多数组织并不是像超大规模企业那样构建的，而且许多可用的推理基础设施都假设它们是这样的。

第一个挑战是身体上的。 大多数企业、电信公司和政府已经拥有数据中心。 他们不能等待两到三年，也不能花费 6 亿多美元购买新设备，而且他们无法在不付出重大成本和中断的情况下进行液体冷却改造。

因此，实际的问题是推理硬件是否运行在他们已有的基础上：标准机架、空气冷却和现有的功率预算。

第二是主权。 组织越来越希望将计算带到数据已经存在的地方，而不是将敏感数据移动到托管计算的地方。

这部分是监管性的，部分是运营性的，但无论哪种方式，仅云推理都会造成许多运营商不再适应的依赖。

我们专门针对这一差距而构建。 我们的系统在标准风冷基础设施上以每台服务器 4-5kW 的功率运行，无需重新设计设施。

SK Telecom 在我们的硬件上运行了近三年，从一个小型集群扩展到接近 100 个机架，现在每天处理 5000 万个 API 事务，完全在其现有网络内进行。

KT Cloud 在全国高速公路闭路电视系统上运行实时推理。 两者都表明，您不需要超大规模的基础设施来以超大规模相关的数量运行人工智能。

  • Cerebras 的 IPO 以及该领域其他公司的潜在上市，使人工智能基础设施成为人们关注的焦点。 这些首次公开募股向市场发出了什么信号？炒作可能在哪些方面超过部署现实？

它告诉公开市场，人工智能基础设施是一种持久的、可投资的资产类别，而不仅仅是风险投资支持的赌注。 这种验证有利于整个行业，包括我们：它表明专用人工智能芯片是真实的，与通用 GPU 不同，并且值得独立资本。

资本流入该行业是必要的，但它本身并不能决定谁会获胜。 定义这个市场下一个十年的公司不一定是资金最多的公司。

他们将是具有真正基础的人：生产客户、部署规模、经过验证的经济性、持久的供应链关系。 这是与筹款规模不同的过滤器，一旦公开市场审查开始，这才是重要的。

自 2020 年以来，我们一直在朝着这个目标迈进，在行业其他公司争夺同样的分配之前，我们就与代工厂和内存合作伙伴建立了生产部署和供应关系。 对于每个认真推理的人来说，首都都是顺风。

它是否得到良好部署是一个单独的问题，市场将在未来几年内给出答案。

  • 展望未来，您在未来 12-24 个月内最密切关注人工智能基础设施和推理的哪些趋势？

现有基础设施内部的扩建不断加速。 大多数企业、电信公司和政府都不会等待新的数据中心。

他们正在将推理部署到已有的设施中，我预计这将成为更大的故事，尽管它比超大规模的头条新闻受到的关注要少。

此外，内存仍然是物理限制。 HBM 供应尚未跟上需求，并且随着模型不断向万亿参数混合专家架构发展，这种压力非但没有减轻，反而增加了。

拥有稳定的战略供应关系的公司将在未来两年内拥有真正的优势，而不仅仅是成本优势。

Chiplet 是我们实现这一目标的方式。 我们已经批量生产了高度先进的 4-chiplet 封装 - Nvidia 一直难以达到的集成水平。

今年的报告表明，Nvidia 已经构建并展示了四芯片组 Rubin Ultra 设计，然后由于可制造性问题而取消了该设计，转而采用双芯片架构：四芯片单封装在产量和成本方面突破了光罩限制约 7.5-8 倍。 这就是基础。

我们正在构建的下一层是 HMB3E（3D 堆栈内存）的性能优化，与内存和计算密切合作，从一开始就共同设计，而不是事后附加。

我注意到的另一个事实是，随着该领域越来越多的公司上市，资本将根据生产基本面而不是融资轮次进行估值。

效率点很重要：随着每个代币的推理变得更便宜，需求不会缩小，而是会扩大，因为新的用例以更低的成本变得可行。 历史上的每个计算平台都是如此，我不认为人工智能推理会例外。
